design_summary.purpose: Synthesizable FPGA control shell for an external compact aerodynamics surrogate worker. The top-level provides firmware-visible CSR/MMIO control and status, compact request/response transport supervision, timeout and stale-data handling, bounded actuator-command output, and fault-safe inhibition behavior. It does not implement inference internally; it supervises external compact decisions and gates actuator validity on invalid, stale, reset, timeout, or fault conditions.
design_summary.operating_model: Single-clock synchronous design on clk with synchronous reset_n. Firmware configures control, timeout, staleness, and actuator clamp policy through the CSR/MMIO window. The transport supervisor emits compact 64-bit request metadata, accepts compact 64-bit response metadata, validates sequencing and freshness, clamps accepted actuator commands, and inhibits actuator validity when supervision rules are violated. Optional BRAM-backed buffering is handled by a technology-neutral memory wrapper and is not a software-visible substitute for the CSR interface.

external_interfaces.name: firmware CSR/MMIO window
external_interfaces.summary: 64-bit register-mapped interface with csr_addr[7:0], csr_wdata[63:0], csr_rdata[63:0], csr_we, csr_re, csr_valid, csr_ready, and deterministic response semantics. It exposes control, status, timeout, stale, clamp, sequence, and fault/diagnostic registers.

external_interfaces.name: compact external model transport
external_interfaces.summary: 64-bit request/response sideband for compact metadata only. The design drives stream_out_valid/data and consumes stream_out_ready for request emission; it consumes stream_in_valid/data and drives stream_in_ready for response acceptance. No wide geometry or field payloads are exposed.

external_interfaces.name: actuator command outputs
external_interfaces.summary: Registered compact actuator_cmd[31:0] and actuator_cmd_valid outputs, plus fault_code[7:0] and safe-fallback status semantics via status/fault indicators. Command validity is inhibited on reset, invalid data, timeout, stale data, malformed packets, or fault latch conditions.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_control_top
module_architecture.role: Top-level synthesizable control shell that integrates CSR/MMIO, transport supervision, optional buffering, and externally visible command/fault outputs.
responsibilities: Provide a real firmware-visible CSR/MMIO interface with address, write-data, read-data, valid, write-enable, read-enable, and ready/response semantics.
Expose CSR registers for operating mode, timeout threshold, stale threshold, actuator minimum and maximum limits, request sequence seed, last command, and fault/diagnostic flags.
Emit compact 64-bit model-request metadata on stream_out_data with stream_out_valid and accept backpressure on stream_out_ready.
Receive compact 64-bit model-response metadata on stream_in_data with stream_in_valid and advertise readiness on stream_in_ready only when the parser can accept a full word.
Validate sequence numbers, reject malformed or out-of-order responses, and detect stale or timed-out transactions.
Clamp command outputs to programmable actuator limits and assert actuator_cmd_valid only for accepted commands.
Assert fault_code when safety violations occur.
Reset into inhibited safe state with actuator_cmd_valid deasserted and CSR-backed configuration/status defaults loaded.
Maintain transparent reference/status visibility through CSR-readable status words and last accepted sequence tracking.
interface_notes: Top-level ports are fixed by the spec and include clk, reset_n, CSR control, compact streaming, actuator outputs, fault_code, and buf_dout.
External model transport direction follows the mandatory contract: request valid/data are outputs, request ready is an input; response valid/data are inputs, response ready is an output.
The top-level output ports must be real RTL-driven signals; no required output is satisfied by a child input-only connection.
ownership_notes: Owns the overall system contract for firmware control, transport supervision, safety inhibition, and command visibility.
Does not own inference; it only supervises and relays compact control decisions from external software/firmware.
Does not rename hierarchy, ports, or filenames; rtl_output_file remains adaptive_aero_control_top.v.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_csr_mmio
module_architecture.role: Firmware-visible CSR/MMIO register block and sole software-facing configuration/status source.
responsibilities: Decode address 0x00 control, 0x08 status, 0x10 timeout_limit, 0x18 stale_limit, 0x20 actuator_min, 0x28 actuator_max, 0x30 last_command, and 0x38 fault_code/diagnostic flags.
Provide a real ready/response MMIO handshake using csr_valid, csr_ready, csr_re, and csr_rdata.
Publish semantic control outputs to the transport/safety supervisor.
Expose current status and diagnostic readbacks with exact CSR field semantics.
Support explicit fault clear and sequence-seed programming from firmware.
interface_notes: Writable fields drive semantic control outputs consumed by the supervisor; read-only fields are produced by the supervisor and made software-visible through CSR readback.
The register contract is authoritative and every declared register must be reachable through RTL decode.
csr_ready indicates acceptance/consumption of a CSR transaction; csr_rdata carries deterministic readback for the addressed register.
ownership_notes: Owns the implemented register map described in DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.register_contract.
Owns the firmware-visible view of enable, mode, clear_fault, sequence seed, timeout/stale limits, actuator clamps, last_command, and fault/diagnostic status.
Does not own transport or actuator outputs directly; it provides control/status semantics to the supervisor and accepts its status feedback.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_transport_supervisor
module_architecture.role: Enumerated transport and safety FSM that supervises compact request/response exchange and bounded actuator command generation.
responsibilities: Generate 64-bit compact request metadata with monotonically increasing sequence tracking.
Accept only 64-bit compact response metadata words and validate format/sequence/freshness.
Drive fault_present and fault_code on timeout, malformed packet, stale response, or sequence mismatch.
Clamp accepted command values to cfg_actuator_min and cfg_actuator_max.
Publish status_ready, timeout status, last accepted sequence, last command, and diagnostic flags to the CSR block.
Assert actuator_cmd_valid only for accepted and bounded commands.
Support explicit clear_fault acknowledgement path.
Prioritize safety over latency and never emit unvalidated actuator commands.
interface_notes: Uses enumerated FSM states IDLE, ISSUE_REQ, WAIT_RESP, VALIDATE, APPLY_CMD, and FAULT_LATCH, with one-hot or equivalent synthesizable encoding.
Request output remains asserted until req_ready or until timeout aborts the transaction.
rsp_ready only asserts when the parser can accept a full compact response word.
The block consumes firmware configuration inputs and returns supervisory status outputs to CSR/MMIO.
All externally visible command outputs are registered.
No silent replacement of requested commands is permitted on invalid data; invalid data must inhibit actuator_cmd_valid and raise fault state.
ownership_notes: Owns request issuance, response acceptance, sequence checking, timeout/staleness tracking, saturation diagnostics, and fault-latched inhibition behavior.
Does not perform surrogate inference; it only handles compact control decisions returned by external software.
Does not own software-visible register decode; it reports status and accepts configuration from the CSR block.

module_architecture.name: adaptive_aero_buffer_controller
module_architecture.role: Technology-neutral buffer controller for optional compact history or diagnostics storage mapped to FPGA block RAM.
responsibilities: Expose a narrow compact buffering interface suitable for block RAM mapping.
Avoid any register-file substitution for bulk storage.
Derive buffer control from buf_addr and buf_we while preserving the declared interface semantics.
Support optional readback of compact history data into a top-level observable path without altering the transport/safety contract.
Implement bulk storage as an inferred memory rather than a flattened bank of scalar registers.
Return stored read data through the declared functional output port.
interface_notes: Acts as the bridge between compact history/buffer semantics and the underlying BRAM wrapper.
buf_dout is functionally observable through the top-level input port and is not a decorative or disconnected signal.
Reset disables buffer access and leaves storage contents implementation-defined for FPGA block RAM mapping.
ownership_notes: Owns optional history/diagnostic buffering only, not the CSR contract or actuator control.
Must remain technology-neutral and FPGA-friendly; no Sky130 macro or ASIC memory construct is used in the FPGA path.
Bulk payload/history/FIFO storage is described through an inferred memory wrapper and not flattened into registers.

module_architecture.name: generic_fpgabrams_64x64
module_architecture.role: Declared technology-neutral inferred FPGA block RAM wrapper for optional history buffering.
responsibilities: Provide the explicit memory wrapper instance for FPGA synthesis flow mapping.
Accept write controls and address/data inputs from the buffer controller.
Drive read data that is consumed by the buffer controller.
Implement bulk storage as an inferred memory rather than a flattened bank of scalar registers.
Return stored read data through the declared functional output port.
interface_notes: Native BRAM-style port set: clk, csb, we, addr, din, dout.
The wrapper is functionally consumed by adaptive_aero_buffer_controller via sram_dout and exists to satisfy the FPGA memory contract.
It is not decorative and is the sole memory primitive described for the FPGA path.
ownership_notes: Owns the technology-neutral memory abstraction used for optional buffering.
Does not participate in CSR/MMIO decode or actuator control.
Must remain an inferred-memory abstraction compatible with FPGA block RAM mapping.

interface_summary.intent: Firmware issues CSR/MMIO transactions into the register block for configuration and status readback.
Register block returns acceptance/response semantics and read data to software.
Firmware-programmed control and policy fields are consumed by the transport/safety supervisor.
Supervisory state and diagnostic status are made software-visible through CSR readback.
The top-level emits compact 64-bit request metadata toward the external worker.
Backpressure on request transport is consumed by the supervisor.
The top-level receives compact 64-bit response metadata from the external worker.
Response readiness is asserted only when a full compact response word can be accepted.
Registered bounded actuator command and its validity are driven as the final external command interface.
Latched fault code is exported for software handling and system-level safety response.
Current request sequencing and compact history indexing semantics may be used to steer optional buffering.
Compact request metadata can be captured into optional history storage.
The buffer controller drives the inferred FPGA block RAM wrapper with narrow memory controls.
Block RAM read data is consumed by the buffer controller as sram_dout.
Optional buffer readback is made functionally observable at the top level without replacing the CSR interface.

data_flow_summary: Firmware configures enable, mode, fault-clear, sequence seed, timeout and staleness thresholds, and actuator clamp limits through the CSR/MMIO block.
The transport supervisor uses those policy values to issue a compact 64-bit request word and to validate incoming 64-bit response metadata from the external worker.
The request path maintains valid until ready or timeout abort; the response path asserts ready only when the parser can accept a full compact word.
Validated response metadata produces a bounded actuator command, which is clamped between programmable minimum and maximum limits before being registered at the top-level command output.

On invalid, stale, malformed, duplicate, out-of-order, or timed-out conditions, actuator_cmd_valid is inhibited and fault_code is latched for software handling; no silent substitute command is emitted.
Optional compact history can be captured in BRAM-backed storage through the buffer controller and exposed via buf_dout, but it does not replace the CSR/MMIO control-plane or transport contract.

clock_reset_summary.clocking: Single clock domain clk at 50.0 MHz. All sequential logic is synchronous to clk. Outputs that leave the chip or are visible at the top level are registered where specified by the architecture.
clock_reset_summary.reset_behavior: reset_n is active-low and synchronous. On reset, the design enters an inhibited safe state with actuator command validity deasserted, transient transport state cleared, and CSR-backed configuration/status registers initialized to defined defaults. Safety behavior prioritizes inhibition over any command emission on reset release. The descriptive architecture remains aligned with the spec's control-first safety contract and does not introduce hierarchy, ports, or filenames outside DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON.

integration_notes: The firmware control plane is mandatory and coexists with the streaming transport; it does not get replaced by transport-only supervision.
The external model transport direction contract is applied by data flow: request valid/data are outputs and request ready is an input; response valid/data are inputs and response ready is an output.
A top-level output must be driven by real RTL logic; required outputs are not satisfied by child inputs alone.
The CSR register map in register_contract is the authoritative software-visible interface and every listed register is reachable through RTL decode.
The FPGA memory contract is satisfied by a technology-neutral inferred-memory wrapper for bulk history/buffer storage; bulk storage is not flattened into registers.
No command fallback substitution is permitted on invalid, stale, timeout, reset, or fault conditions; command validity is inhibited and the fault is latched for software handling.
The architecture preserves compact transport only; it does not expose wide geometry arrays, pressure fields, or flow fields at top level.
State machines are described as enumerated and synthesizable, with synchronous reset and no inferred latches.
The top-level port count remains compact and below the specified scalar-equivalent I/O ceiling, with streaming and register-mapped widths within the stated limits.
consistency_notes: No hierarchy, ports, or filenames may differ from digital_spec_json.
DIGITAL_SPEC_JSON is the single source of truth; this output preserves the specified module responsibilities and inter-module contracts without redefining them.
The top module remains adaptive_aero_control_top and is not substituted by a status, telemetry, register-bank, or leaf module.
